comment: Reads straight from notes, hard to hear through mask, thankfully its not complex material. Exams often don't reflect what's actually taught. Frequently brings up political views that have no place in a Torts class. Overall, class felt disorganized and unproductive. Would not recommend but you probably have no other option.

You either love him or you hate him. If you jive well with him, you'll love him. But to be a good professor, you need to be able to reach all your students, his voice alone only reaches the first row. He's knowledgable, but quiet and boring. You'll be better off doing independent research on con law history than wasting time going to class.

He is a fantastic professor and regarded as one of the highest authorities in Torts.  The lectures are important because it helps to solidify what you learn in the readings but he sometime lets the class get on tangents which takes time away from the focus of the course.  He did not cold call but extra points given for participation.
He's smart, no doubt about it, but you need to sit in the first two rows of the classroom to be able to listen and understand

What to say about Toby? Undeniably brilliant, super nice, genuinely cares about his students, his pants stay up by some force that defies gravity, and very willing to help. That being said he is very dry at times. However, if you pay attention you will learn he is actually quite funny, but his quips will be missed if you blink. No cold-calling too!
Brilliant Man in addition to being extremely helpful and respectful of his students. Also his final in Constitutional Law is fairly straight forward.

He's brilliant, well respected, absolutely respectful of students (not common at this Law School) but also incredibly boring. You can tell he's an "academic", and has probably never been in a courtroom, outside of clerking for someone. But still, a good professor overall and fair grader.

Prof. Tobias is a fair professor. He is extremely bright. The beauty of Prof. Tobias is that he does not speak down to students and and not arrogant. He is interested in your comments and thoughts and is quite funny, if you pay attention. Exams not bad!
Professor Tobias is very bright without being arrogant: a rare combination in the law and at law schools.
Very dry presentation and very dry wit.  Maggie is entertaining, and the tests fair.

Professor Tobias and his little dog Maggie. He may not be the most effective professor but he is extremely intelligent and one of the nicest professors you will ever have. His dog is also really sweet, that alone should earn him a good ranking.
